newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PM SAYS PLANS FOR NO MORE IMF LOANS.
newsitem.headline: PM SAYS PLANS FOR NO MORE IMF LOANS.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that the Baltic state did not plan to commit itself to more loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"When cooperating with the IMF in the future we will never commit ourselves to any credit line or separate loans," Vagnorius said at a news conference.
"Lithuania is becoming a state which is capable of cooperating with the IMF and the World Bank in a more profitable and effective way," he added.
Lithuania's current three-year memorandum with the IMF ends in September.
The fund's relationship with Vagnorius' government has been strained by disagreements over agriculture tariffs and the future of monetary policy.
But Vagnorius said that the two sides had patched up their differences and signed a letter of intent on Wednesday.
"We are glad that we reached agreement and don't have to reduce import tariffs for agricultural goods," he said.

"The IMF also agreed with our plan to gradually remove the currency board model and restore the (monetary) functions of the central bank...and the transition from the mechanically fixed mechanism to a more liberal fix," he added.
The government and central bank plan to scrap the currency board, which pegs the litas to the dollar at a rate of four to one, in three stages over the next three years.
The first stage will begin with repo auctions in April.
"I want to say that there will be no changes to the litas rate this year," he said.
"In the future, probably in 1998...the litas rate change will depend on inflation," he said.
